title: Applied ML Eval Harness, Prompt Sets, Onboarding, Guardrails, Quantization & Regression Playbook
author: Jordan Kim
content:
Overview

This playbook consolidates our canonical standards and operational procedures for applied ML evaluations at Redwood Inference. It covers: the eval-harness architecture and ownership, prompt set and benchmark guidelines, model onboarding checklist, quality guardrails, quantization profile best practices, and a step-by-step regression triage playbook. Use this document as the single source of truth for cross-functional onboarding, release gating, and post-release regression response.

Scope and goals
- Scope: internal evals used for model onboarding, release verification, and continuous monitoring for hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
- Goals: reproducible evals, early detection of quality regressions, automated gating for model rollouts, and clear escalation paths.

Owner & contacts
- Primary owner: Applied ML + Eval team (engineering).
- Runtime/Serving contact: Runtime Performance team.
- Oncall escalation: eng-sre oncall (see oncall roster link).

1) Eval-harness: architecture & standards
Intro: Our eval-harness provides deterministic, instrumented evaluation runs against curated prompt sets and metrics collectors. The harness is implemented as a dockerized runner with reproducible seeds, deterministic tokenization settings, and standardized metric exporters.

Key principles:
- Repeatability: every run must declare seed, model version, model config, and harness version.
- Observability: all runs must export per-example outputs, latencies, and per-metric breakdowns to the metrics store.
- Modularity: metric calculators and prompt set loaders are pluggable.

Minimal run metadata (REQUIRED):
- run_id (uuid)
- harness_version (semver)
- model_name and model_version (exact model id used in serving)
- prompt_set_id (see Prompt Set Catalog)
- random_seed
- hardware_profile (cpu, gpu type)
- quantization_profile (if applicable)

Standard SLOs for eval-harness runs:
- Successful completion rate >= 99.5% (no crashed tasks)
- Metadata completeness >= 100%
- Per-example output retention: 30 days in experiments bucket

Example CLI
- docker run --rm -e MODEL=redwood-v1-eval:2026-10-01 -v $(pwd)/outputs:/outputs eval-harness:stable 
  --prompt-set prompt_set_id --seed 42 --out /outputs/${MODEL}_results.json

2) Prompt Set and Benchmark Guidelines
Overview: Prompt sets represent the single-source canonical test inputs used for onboarding and regression testing. Each prompt set is versioned, tagged with domains, and accompanied by annotation schemas and reference outputs where relevant.

Prompt set metadata (minimum):
- id, name, version, domain_tags (e.g., summarization, code, qa), size (count), per-example metadata (difficulty, expected_behavior)
- intended_use: onboarding | gating | continuous-monitoring

Design guidelines:
- Coverage: the set should cover common user intents, edge cases, and adversarial examples. Aim for 60/30/10 split: 60% common, 30% edge, 10% adversarial.
- Balanced distribution: avoid single-domain dominance unless the set is domain-specific.
- Annotation: each example must include a short rationale and primary failure modes to expect.

Benchmarking metrics (examples):
- Automated: BLEU/ROUGE (where applicable), exact-match, embedding-similarity (cosine), token-level perplexity, hallucination-score heuristic.
- Human-in-the-loop: succinctness, factuality, helpfulness ratings (1-5).

Example prompt-set entry (text):
- id: ps-2026-README-summaries-v1
- domain_tags: ["summarization", "news"]
- size: 1,200

3) Model onboarding checklist (gate for serving)
Use this checklist for every new model/version before it is allowed into canary or production routing. Each item must be signed off and logged in the model-onboarding ticket.

Gating items:
1. Automated evals: run full eval-harness against onboarding prompt sets and continuous-monitoring prompt sets.
   - Pass criteria: no metric regression > 2.5% on critically monitored metrics; no single critical example failure where output is unsafe or toxic.
2. Latency/cost baseline: run perf-suite for representative sequence lengths.
   - Target p50 latency <= target_latency_table[profile] and token cost within 10% of baseline.
3. Quantization validation: if using int8/4-bit profile, run quantization profile tests (see section 5).
4. Safety scan: automated safety filters + manual review by Safety SME for high-risk domains.
5. E2E integration smoke: API contract tests, streaming behavior test, and function-calling semantics validated.
6. Monitoring hooks: ensure logging, metrics, and tracing are configured; add model version and prompt_set tags.
7. Rollout plan: staged canary (5% -> 25% -> 100%), rollback criteria, and owner for each step.

4) Quality guardrails and monitoring
Objective: detect silent quality regressions and limit user-facing impact.

Guardrail categories:
- Static guardrails: safety filters, toxic-content blocklists, forbidden-action detectors.
- Dynamic guardrails: drift detectors, metric-based SLO alerts (e.g., helpfulness score drop), and per-customer QA monitors for enterprise tenants.

Alerting thresholds (examples):
- Critical: aggregated helpfulness score drop > 8% over a 24 hour window OR high-confidence hallucination rate > 5%
- Major: aggregated latency p95 increase > 40% OR error-rate increase > 2pp

Mitigations and automatic responses:
- Automated fallback: route traffic to previous model-version or cheaper model-variant when critical alert fires.
- Canary pause: halt rollout progression and notify owners.
- Throttle: reduce concurrent batch sizes for affected routes to stabilize latency.

5) Quantization profiles & validation
Purpose: provide repeatable quantization configurations and validation steps for different model classes to balance cost vs quality.

Profile naming convention: qp-<model-family>-<bits>-<date> (e.g., qp-llama2-4bit-2026-06-01)

Profile metadata (required):
- model_family, bits, backend (e.g., triton, onnxruntime, custom-kernel), calibration_dataset_id, notes_on_known_regressions

Validation steps:
1. Calibration pass: run calibration on calibration_dataset_id, save calibration artifacts.
2. Unit evals: run eval-harness subset (representative 200 examples) and compare deltas to fp16 baseline.
   - Acceptable maximum degradation: 1.5% absolute on primary metric for production profiles; 3.5% for cost-optimized profiles (with documented tradeoffs).
3. Latency/cost measurement: measure token throughput and infer per-token cost estimate.
4. Stress test: run long-duration throughput test (>= 4 hours) to detect numerical drift or memory leaks.

Example quantization-policy table (described):
- Production: qp-*-8bit, delta_primary_metric <= 0.8%, used for SLA-critical customers.
- Cost-optimized: qp-*-4bit, delta_primary_metric <= 3.5%, used for batch-only or non-SLA workloads.

6) Regression triage playbook (operational procedure)
Purpose: triage and resolve quality regressions detected by automated or human reporters.

Fast triage (first 30 minutes):
1. Gather context: run-identifiers, model version, prompt_set_id, run artifacts, recent deployment/change log.
2. Reproduce: run failing examples in the eval-harness against the active model-version and the previous good-version.
3. Severity assessment: determine user-impact (number of customers affected, safety implications).
4. Immediate mitigations: if critical, trigger automated fallback and page oncall.

Root cause analysis (next 4 hours):
- Compare per-example token-deltas and log-likelihood traces.
- Check for correlated infra events: GPU driver updates, kernel changes, quantization-profile application, or serving-runtime changes.
- If regression correlates to model change: assess model weights, tokenizer differences, or fine-tune data drift.
- If regression correlates to infra/runtime: attempt a rollback of the runtime change in a canary and validate.

Resolution and rollback criteria:
- Rollback if: majority of critical examples regress AND automated metrics cross critical thresholds OR significant safety failures.
- Hotfix path: if regression is small but widespread, deploy quantization profile rollback or routing policy to route high-risk routes to a protected model-version.

Postmortem and follow-up (within 72 hours):
- Owner prepares a postmortem with timeline, root cause, fix, and action items.
- Required action items: expand prompt-set with failing examples, update quantization profile notes if relevant, add monitoring hooks or new gating checks to prevent recurrence.

Appendix: templates, CLI snippets and example JSON/YAML
- Eval-harness run example (JSON metadata):
  {
    "run_id": "<uuid>",
    "harness_version": "v1.3.0",
    "model_name": "redwood-instruct-1",
    "model_version": "2026-10-01",
    "prompt_set_id": "ps-2026-core-1",
    "random_seed": 42
  }

- Example quantization validation command:
  $ python quantize.py --model redwood-instruct-1 --bits 4 --calibration-dataset ps-quant-calib-2026 --out qp-redwood-4bit-2026-11-01

- Regression triage checklist (short):
  1) Reproduce in harness
  2) Compare to previous good-version
  3) Check infra change log
  4) Apply mitigations (fallback/rollback)
  5) Postmortem and follow-up
